rules.title: RSO annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: If your unit is covered by the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, your landlord can raise the rent only once every 12 months, and only by the percentage LAHD publishes for that year. When a tenant moves out voluntarily or is evicted for certain reasons, the landlord can reset the rent to market rate.
rules.key_value: Once every 12 months by the LAHD-published allowable percentage
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental properties in the City of Los Angeles first built on or before October 1, 1978 (apartments, duplexes, two or more single-family dwellings on one parcel, condos/townhomes, ADUs/JADUs, units attached to commercial buildings), plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28.
rules.exemptions: Condos and townhomes: rent amount not regulated for tenancies that began after December 31, 1995. Luxury exemption is available on application, based on rent charged on or before May 31, 1978. Rent can be reset to market rate after a voluntary move-out, certain evictions, or a buyout.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Municipal Code Ch. XV, Art. 1 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance)

rules.title: RSO: no additional increase for utilities (Feb 2026)
rules.requirement: From February 2, 2026, landlords of RSO units cannot add an extra percentage on top of the annual allowable increase for utilities.
rules.key_value: Utility add-on percentage eliminated as of 2026-02-02
rules.coverage_conditions: RSO units (first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units).
rules.citation: Los Angeles Municipal Code Ch. XV (Rent Stabilization Ordinance), as amended
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.

rules.title: RSO: no 10% increase for added dependents; 10% allowed for added non-dependent tenant
rules.requirement: From February 2, 2026, your landlord cannot charge a 10% increase when a dependent joins your household. The landlord may charge 10% for an additional tenant who is not a dependent, but must do so within 60 days of learning about that tenant.
rules.key_value: 10% for an additional non-dependent tenant, within 60 days; none for dependents
rules.citation: Los Angeles Municipal Code Ch. XV (Rent Stabilization Ordinance), as amended
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted.

rules.title: RSO just-cause eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Your landlord can evict you from an RSO unit only for a listed reason. At-fault reasons include nonpayment, a lease violation, nuisance, illegal use, or refusing access. No-fault reasons include owner or family move-in, a resident manager, demolition, a government order, or conversion to affordable housing. For a no-fault eviction the landlord must file a declaration with LAHD, give 30-, 60- or 120-day written notice, pay relocation assistance, and file the termination notice with LAHD within 3 business days of serving it.
rules.key_value: Enumerated just causes; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the RSO (first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units).
rules.quoted_span: Types of evictions requiring payment of tenant relocation assistance

rules.title: Just Cause Ordinance for non-RSO rental units
rules.requirement: Even if your unit is not rent-stabilized, the Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance protects you against eviction without a legal reason.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units in the City of Los Angeles not covered by the RSO. This page gives no further detail.
rules.citation: LAMC Ch. XVI, Art. 5 (§ 165.00 et seq.)

rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO units must pay tenants interest on their security deposits.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Municipal Code Ch. XV (Rent Stabilization Ordinance)
